claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start by asking: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a son named Alex who's 18 years old. He still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand his current situation.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** 

For example, is he studying for A-levels, doing a vocational course at college, or in any other form of approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in full-time education, I need to understand when his course started and when it ends.

**When did Alex's A-level course start, and when is it scheduled to finish?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He started his A-levels in September last year, so that would be September 2023. The course is due to finish in June this year - June 2024.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning he lives with you and you're responsible for his upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He lives here at home with me, and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is Alex under 20 years old?** (I know he's 18, but I need to confirm his exact age or date of birth to be precise about the age limit rules.)

Also, **are you or Alex currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is 18, so he's definitely under 20. And yes, we both live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I just need to check one more important detail before I can assess your eligibility.

**Does anyone else also claim Child Benefit for Alex, or is there another person who could potentially claim for him (such as another parent or guardian)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, there is another person - Alex's other parent. We're both responsible for Alex, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. That's part of why I'm trying to figure this out.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's an important detail. Let me ask a clarifying question to help assess this situation:

**Does Alex spend equal time living with both of you, or does he primarily live with you? And if he lives primarily with you, do you know approximately how much time he spends with each of you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex lives with me full-time. He's here at home with me all the time - this is his primary residence. The other parent doesn't live with us.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me just check the official guidance to ensure I give you accurate information about your situation, particularly regarding the rules when both parents are responsible but the child lives primarily with one parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. Based on the information you've provided and the official guidance I've reviewed, I can now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

One final question before I provide my assessment: **Has the other parent already made a claim for Child Benefit for Alex, or are they currently receiving Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they haven't made a claim yet. That's why we're in this situation where we can't agree on who should claim it - neither of us has actually claimed it so far.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Alex meets the age and education requirements** - He's 18 (under 20) and studying for A-levels, which counts as approved full-time non-advanced education.

✓ **You meet the responsibility requirement** - Alex lives with you full-time and you're responsible for him.

✓ **You both live in the UK** - This satisfies the residence requirement.

✓ **No duplicate claim exists** - While both you and Alex's other parent are responsible for him, no one has claimed Child Benefit yet.

**Important points to note:**

- Since Alex lives with you full-time, you have a strong basis to make the claim.
- Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child. The guidance says if two people are responsible for the same child, you should agree between yourselves who will claim.
- If both you and the other parent try to claim and cannot agree, HMRC will decide who receives it - but typically it goes to the person the child lives with.

You can go ahead and make your claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Remember, Child Benefit will continue as long as Alex remains in approved education and is under 20 years old, so it should continue until his A-levels finish in June 2024.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?

3. Residence: Both the claimant and Alex live in the UK (Manchester), which satisfies the residence requirement.

4. Responsibility: The claimant confirms that Alex lives with them full-time at home and they are responsible for him, which satisfies the responsibility requirement.

5. According to the guidance, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and if two people are responsible for the same child, they should agree between themselves who will claim. If they cannot agree, HMRC will decide. However, since Alex lives with the claimant full-time and no claim has been made yet, the claimant is eligible to make a claim.

The claimant meets all the eligibility criteria and can make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If the other parent also tries to claim, HMRC will help decide who should receive it, but typically the person the child lives with would be the one to receive it.
